steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The exposure triangle: aperture (f-stop), shutter speed and ISO work together — changing one affects the others. | Key Fact: Aperture controls depth of field: wide aperture (f/1.8) = shallow DoF; narrow aperture (f/16) = deep DoF. | Key Fact: Shutter speed controls motion: fast (1/1000s) freezes action; slow (1/15s) creates blur and sense of movement. | Key Fact: ISO controls sensor sensitivity: low ISO (100) = clean image; high ISO (3200+) = noisy/grainy but usable in low light.
